changes.before: Implement extend as a nonmutating replacement and use it to add five minutes per click.
changes.after: To update an object in state, make a new object with the changed field.

before: Treat an object already in state as read-only. A replacement object allows the next render to use new data without changing the previous object. Object spread {...plan} copies its own enumerable fields into a new object; the later minutes field replaces only that copied value.

extend(plan) accepts a record and returns a new record with five extra minutes. It does not modify the input. setPlan(current => extend(current)) bases each click on the pending state. Spread is shallow: nested objects would still be shared, so changing a nested field requires copying each changed level. These examples use only flat fields.

Optional practice: Add an unchanged flat label field and check that extend preserves it. The checks cover these finite behaviors; a matching DOM alone does not prove every implementation choice. The frame supplies React and mounts App. No imports, server, persistence or network are involved.
after: Treat an object already in state as read-only. Make a new object for the next state. This lets you change one field without rewriting the earlier object.
`{...plan}` copies the plan's fields into a new object. Writing `minutes` after the spread replaces that copied field. Fields written later win when names match.
The name stays the same because the spread copies it. This copy is shallow: objects inside the plan would still be shared. If you change a nested field, copy that inner object too.
Complete `extend` so it returns a new plan with five more minutes. Use it in the state update. Keep every other field and leave the input object unchanged.

before.question: If {...plan, minutes: 15} becomes {minutes: 15, ...plan} and plan.minutes is 10, what value wins?
choices: Both values exist under the same key
before.explanation: Object fields written later overwrite earlier fields with the same key. Spreading plan last restores its old minutes value.

after.question: plan.minutes is 10. What does `{minutes: 15, ...plan}` keep for minutes?
choices: Both numbers under the same field name.
after.explanation: The spread comes last, so it replaces 15 with the plan's old value, 10.

project.title: Replace a field without rewriting the old object
project.task: Make extend return a new plan with five extra minutes. Use it for every Add five click.
project.done_when: The screen adds five each time. Other fields are kept, and earlier objects stay unchanged.
